text: Photosynthesis is a fundamental biological process that allows plants to convert light energy into chemical energy. It is important to note that this process occurs primarily in the chloroplasts, which contain a green pigment called chlorophyll. There are two main stages involved: the light-dependent reactions and the Calvin cycle. During the light-dependent reactions, water molecules are split, releasing oxygen as a byproduct. Subsequently, the Calvin cycle uses the resulting energy carriers to fix carbon dioxide into glucose. Overall, photosynthesis plays a crucial role in sustaining life on Earth by producing both oxygen and the organic compounds that form the base of most food chains.

text: The tricky part wasn't the parser, it was cache invalidation across the two stores. We had a write-through cache in front of Postgres and a separate read replica that the analytics job hammered every fifteen minutes. Under load the replica lag would spike to eight or nine seconds, and any request that landed in that window would read a stale row, write a derived value based on it, and then the write-through would happily persist the wrong number. Took us two weeks to find because it only reproduced under concurrent load, and our staging environment ran a single instance.
